transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Diaz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Spectra), Priya Raman (ML Engineer), Avery Kim (Product), Sam Ortiz (Infra)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Spectra wants to lift their search relevance for product docs; currently using BM25 + open-source FAISS for nearest-neighbor but recall and tail latency are issues. They are evaluating whether Redwood Hosted can meet latency/cost or if Dedicated/Private is needed for throughput and compliance.

Topics: Vector DB integration, embedding size, throughput, hybrid search, security/SOC2, VPC peering

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Rafael who is our SE. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:08] Jordan: Hey Maya, thanks. Jordan here. We wanted to run through our current stack and see where Redwood fits for embeddings + rerank.
[00:13] Rafael: Great, quick question: are you currently serving embeddings in a vector DB already or are you storing them in house?
[00:17] Priya: We're using FAISS at the moment, self-hosted on k8s, and a little custom plumbing. We do an initial BM25 candidate set from Elasticsearch then rerank with nearest neighbors, but recall drops for long-tail queries.
[00:30] Avery: And cost is creeping up since we're storing high-dim embeddings and doing lots of brute-force searches for reranks.
[00:36] Rafael: Makes sense. What dimensionality are you using now? 768? 512?
[00:40] Priya: Right now it's 768 from a public transformer. We experimented with 256 but saw a small dip in relevance, at least on our metric.
[00:47] Maya: Do you have throughput targets (qps or concurrency) for the rerank step?
[00:50] Jordan: Peak is around 200 qps for user-facing search during our morning window, but sustained baseline is closer to 50 qps. Latency SLO we'd love is sub-200ms tail for the rerank step end-to-end.
[01:05] Rafael: ok, so 200 qps peak. For Hosted we typically suggest batching and prefix caching where possible; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput. Private/VPC helps if you have strict egress policies.
[01:18] Sam: Security wise we need SOC2, encryption at rest and in transit, and a vendor that can do VPC peering; on-prem is a hard requirement for some customers so private deployment is on the table.
[01:30] Maya: We have SOC2, can provide audit logs and KMS integrations. Our Private offering supports customer-controlled networking and we can run an on-prem package in air-gapped environments if needed. I'll share the security whitepaper.
[01:42] Priya: Can you talk about vector DB integrations? We don't want a big rewrite if we move to Redwood for embeddings/serving.
[01:47] Rafael: We integrate with Pinecone and Qdrant out of the box; for FAISS we support bringing precomputed indexes or we can host the index layer. Many teams keep their vector DB and call Redwood for embedding generation + rerank model, or we host the entire serving stack for simpler ops.
[02:02] Jordan: If we keep FAISS, what changes: do we push embeddings from Redwood or pull?
[02:06] Rafael: You can do either. Typical flow: Redwood generates embeddings via the API, returns vectors which you persist to FAISS. For rerank we support a re-rank endpoint that takes candidates + query and runs a cross-encoder or asymmetric scoring; if you want lower latency we can do approximate ANN on the host side. There's flexibility.
[02:22] Avery: What's the cost tradeoff: Hosted token/embedding costs vs Dedicated reserved GPU costs?
[02:27] Maya: Hosted is easiest to get started; pay-as-you-go per embedding op. Dedicated is priced for committed capacity and tends to be more economical at sustained high qps because you get reserved GPU pools and can control batch sizes. Private adds platform fee and sometimes infra/installation costs. We'll send a comparison sheet.
[02:45] Priya: On dimensionality: if we move to 256 dim vectors from our current 768, what's the typical tradeoff?
[02:50] Rafael: Generally you see lower storage and faster ANN ops at 256 but potentially lower recall for edge cases; depends on the model and your corpus. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dim reduction profiles and we can run A/B evals on your dataset to quantify the regression.
[03:10] Jordan: About rerank model: are you running cross-encoder style rerankers or do you do a separate lightweight scorer?
[03:15] Rafael: We support both. Cross-encoders give the best quality but are compute heavy; we often recommend a two-stage pipeline: BM25 then sparse+dense hybrid for candidate generation, then a small cross-encoder or a distil cross-encoder for rerank. For latency-sensitive flows we can use a learned asymmetric scorer that scores query against precomputed doc representations.
[03:36] Avery: Does Redwood support hybrid search combined with BM25 out of the box?
[03:40] Maya: Yes, many customers keep BM25 for recall and embedding-based ranking for semantic similarity. We have examples and templates showing how to structure the candidate set and the rerank call.
[03:49] Priya: Performance question: if we want to sustain 200 qps with sub-200ms tail, what sort of infra do you need? We're running on GCP with n1 VMs and some T4 nodes for inference.
[04:03] Rafael: For 200 qps with cross-encoder rerank you'd likely need dedicated GPU pools; A100 or H100 for dense cross-encoders, though asymmetric or distilled models can run on T4s or lower-cost GPUs. Batching is key; continuous batching can amortize kernel overhead. We'll propose a config after we run a perf feed with sample queries.
[04:22] Jordan: How do you handle KV cache for chat-like rerank? We have some context windows that need to be preserved.
[04:27] Rafael: We manage KV cache in the runtime; sometimes folks call it KV cache, sometimes KV cash in the transcripts, but we keep track. For rerank it's usually small so cache hit patterns are less of a thing, but for multi-turn contexts we keep the cache per-session and can evict based on policy.
[04:44] Sam: If we go Private, what's the network model? VPC peering or private link?
[04:48] Maya: We support VPC peering and private link options for Private deployments; for Hosted we support dedicated egress IPs and IP allowlists. For on-prem deployed Private, we ship an appliance image that runs behind your firewall. We'll send the network diagram.
[05:03] Priya: Any benchmarks you can share for embeddings QPS and rerank p99 latencies?
[05:08] Rafael: We have publicized numbers on our docs but they're workload-dependent. We'll run a 48-72 hour benchmark using your sample set and measure p50/p90/p99 for both embedding generation and rerank. That will inform whether Hosted can meet your tail latency or Dedicated is required.
[05:22] Avery: What about vector index formats: do you support product like IVF+PQ, HNSW, or others?
[05:27] Rafael: Yes: HNSW, IVF+PQ, OPQ, quantization options are supported depending on the index provider; if you use FAISS we can leverage PQ/OPQ to reduce storage and speed queries. Pinecone/Qdrant have managed options. There's a balance between recall and throughput.
[05:41] Jordan: On the subject of data residency: some customers require EU-only data. Is that possible?
[05:46] Maya: Yes, we have region controls and Private deployments allow you to keep customer data in your VPC/region. Hosted can also pin workloads to region endpoints for EU-only processing but for strict residency we recommend Private.
[05:58] Priya: For our eval metrics: what should we measure? Mean reciprocal rank? Recall@k? nDCG?
[06:02] Rafael: We typically recommend Recall@k for candidate quality and nDCG for ranking quality. Also measure latency p50/p90/p99 and cost per query. Redwood Optimize can track regressions against a baseline prompt set.
[06:16] Maya: Quick note: if you plan to use cross-encoders, count those as heavy ops in cost modeling; we can show cost per 1k queries for different rerank settings.
[06:26] Avery: We're also worried about storage costs for embeddings at 768 dims. How much can quantization help?
[06:31] Rafael: With PQ/8-bit quantization you can often cut storage by 4x with moderate recall hit; 4-bit plus OPQ can be aggressive but you'll want to validate. We'll include sample numbers in the benchmarking doc.
[06:44] Jordan: Operationally, what's the integration work? Is there a customer SDK?
[06:48] Maya: Yes, we have SDKs and a simple REST API. Many customers integrate via SDK for generation and push embeddings into their existing vector DB. For full Redwood-hosted index and rerank, integration is a couple endpoints and an ingestion pipeline. We'll share examples.
[07:02] Priya: If we bring our own FAISS, do you recommend keeping precomputed indexes and incremental upserts?
[07:07] Rafael: Yes, incremental upserts are typical. If you want Redwood to host the index we can offer near-real-time upserts; otherwise you can run FAISS and call our embedding endpoint. We'll discuss options in the benchmark plan.
[07:20] Avery: Any known issues with high-dimensional embeddings and ANN?
[07:23] Rafael: High dimension suffers from curse of dimensionality; ANN algorithms become less discriminative as dim grows and PQ helps. Dimensionality reduction models or distilled encoders often give similar utility at lower cost; Redwood Optimize can evaluate model/dim combos.
[07:36] Jordan: On compliance: does Redwood provide logs for audit and a SOC2 report?
[07:40] Maya: Yes, we provide SOC2 Type II reports on request and can supply audit logs, access logs, and KMS integration info. For Private we can integrate with your existing key management (HSM/KMS).
[07:53] Priya: What about SSO and role-based access?
[07:56] Maya: We support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC in the console. We'll include the docs link.
[08:04] Sam: A nit: do you support bringing your own model weights for private? We have some internal models and want to control weights on-prem.
[08:10] Rafael: For Private deployments you can bring weights; we'd need to validate licensing and compatibility. For Hosted we generally host verified open models and our curated catalog.
[08:22] Avery: Ok, timeline: if we decide to pilot, how fast can we spin up a proof-of-concept?
[08:27] Maya: For Hosted you can get started in days. For Dedicated pilot typically 2-4 weeks to provision reserved capacity. Private depends on the install complexity but we've done on-prem pilots in a few weeks with infra prep. We'll coordinate with Sam.
[08:41] Jordan: Pricing: can you give a ballpark for 200 qps peak with a mix of generation and rerank?
[08:47] Maya: Ballpark depends on model and rerank strategy; we'll provide a scenario-based estimate in the pricing sheet. Dedicated often saves money at sustained load.
[08:57] Priya: One more technical: how do you manage model versions and rollouts? We don't want a surprise regression in production.
[09:03] Rafael: We support model pinning, canary rollouts, and regression alerts tied to eval sets. Redwood Optimize can flag quality regressions and rollback.
[09:14] Avery: Let's capture next steps. Priya will share the dataset and queries; Rafael will draft a benchmark plan; Maya will send security docs and pricing; Sam will connect his infra contact.
[09:25] Jordan: That sounds good. Anything else?
[09:28] Maya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff and send the docs. Thanks all.
[09:33] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:34] Jordan: Thanks.

End of transcript (timestamps are approximate; auto-transcribed text may contain small errors).
